counterexample: Let n=2 and let H have vertices V_H={v1,v2}. The construction gives G with vertices {v1,v2,u1,...,u17}. The set {u1,u2} consists of n=2 distinct vertices of G but contains neither original vertex, directly contradicting the claim that every set of n distinct vertices of G must include all of V_H.
assessment_summary: Step 0033 uses an invalid counting argument: choosing n vertices from n+17 vertices does not force inclusion of all n original vertices. Although the later observation that a multi-vertex path cannot contain isolated vertices could repair the reverse implication for n>1, step 0033 itself is false, so strict step-by-step verification stops there.
